Job Description

General Motors is seeking a Power Electronics Controls Engineer to lead the design and integration of controls for high-voltage power electronics including DC/DC converters, inverters and on-board chargers. You will translate vehicle and electrical-system requirements into robust control strategies, diagnostics, calibration, and verification plans—then drive them through validation and production launch.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role spanning controls architecture, embedded software, hardware integration, laboratory and vehicle testing, supplier direction, and issue resolution.

Role Responsibilities

Define controls architecture and operating modes for voltage/current regulation, power management, startup/shutdown, transitions, derating, protection, and fault recovery.

Derive controller requirements based on system performance requirements and drive controller selection

Translate system requirements into control, software, calibration, diagnostic, and interface requirements.

Balance efficiency, transient response, stability, thermal performance, electromagnetic compatibility, safety, cost, and timing.

Design diagnostic monitoring, fault thresholds, degraded modes, safe-state behavior, and recovery strategies.

Partner with calibration and software teams on parameter definition, tuning, model-based development, test planning, and release readiness.

Lead controls integration across converter hardware, embedded software, battery systems, vehicle energy management, electrical architecture, validation, and vehicle integration.

Plan and review simulation, hardware-in-the-loop, laboratory, and vehicle verification; use objective data to confirm performance and robustness.

Lead root-cause investigations and corrective actions for controls, performance, communication, diagnostic, and vehicle-integration issues.

Provide technical directions to suppliers and review architecture, software maturity, calibration capability, diagnostic coverage, test evidence, and launch readiness.

Communicate technical risks and decisions, influence cross-functional teams, and mentor engineers.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, controls engineering, or a related discipline.

8+ years of relevant experience in power electronics, embedded controls, automotive electrical systems, or electrified-vehicle technologies.

Hands-on experience developing or integrating embedded controls for production DC/DC converters, onboard chargers, or related power-conversion systems.

Strong fundamentals in feedback control, mode management, transient response, stability, protection, derating, diagnostics, and fault handling.

Experience translating system requirements into controls, software, calibration, diagnostics, and verification plans.

Lead collaboration efforts between HW and SW teams by working closely with HW lead to understanding the HW blocks and implementing HW controls while providing defined controls specifications to SW team.

Experience defining or implementing automotive diagnostics, including monitoring, fault detection, diagnostic trouble codes, thresholds, degraded modes, and recovery behavior.

Experience leading technical issue resolution using structured root-cause analysis and objective test data.

Knowledge of CAN, LIN, Ethernet, functional safety, cybersecurity, EMC, electrical transients, or vehicle energy management.

Experience with model-based development, automatic code generation, plant modeling, hardware-in-the-loop testing, or real-time controls simulation.

Ability to coordinate cross-functional technical decisions and influence internal teams and suppliers without direct authority.

Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills.

Willingness to travel periodically to supplier, test, and vehicle-development locations as needed.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree or advanced technical training in electrical engineering, controls, power electronics, computer engineering, or a related field.

10+ years of relevant experience in power electronics, embedded controls, automotive electrical systems, or electrified-vehicle technologies.

Experience with bidirectional on-board chargers or isolated DC/DC converters, high-voltage systems, or low-voltage vehicle networks.

Knowledge of functional safety, cybersecurity, diagnostics standards, electrical transients, electromagnetic compatibility, and vehicle energy-management strategies.

Experience coordinating software, calibration, hardware, and vehicle-integration changes to resolve validation or field issues.

Experience with supplier technical reviews, controls assessments, and production-launch readiness.

Experience with design-for-manufacturing, design-for-service, and controls robustness for high-volume production.

Experience with supplier technical reviews, production launch, and design-for-manufacturing or service.

Candidate Success Profile

The strongest candidate will combine strong controls fundamentals with automotive power electronics hardware knowledge to deliver controls strategies. They will be comfortable moving between controls architecture, calibration, diagnostics, software and hardware integration, laboratory testing, vehicle testing, supplier discussions, and leadership communication.

Success in the first year will include establishing a repeatable power electronics controls development and issue-resolution approach, supporting calibration and diagnostic readiness, providing clear technical directions to suppliers and cross-functional teams, and reduce late-cycle controls issues across the power electronics portfolio.

Job description
A leading organization is seeking a Systems Analyst to support a data annotation and review platform. The Systems Analyst will focus on designing workflows, improving review processes, supporting data movement, and helping technical teams use the platform effectively.

The position will collaborate closely with data science teams to turn operational needs into efficient, well-defined system workflows.
Responsibilities

Design and document data annotation workflows.
Define structured review processes for annotation activities.
Analyze and optimize end-to-end workflows to improve operational efficiency.
Partner with data science teams to support effective tool adoption.
Map data movement and integrations between systems.
Use SQL to support data analysis and workflow requirements.
Develop process and workflow documentation using tools such as Visio.
Help establish consistent processes for moving data into and out of the platform.

Required experience and skills

Experience designing annotation or data-focused workflows.
Experience defining and improving review processes.
Ability to analyze and optimize end-to-end workflows.
SQL experience.
Experience with APIs and data mapping.
Experience using Visio or similar process-mapping tools.
Ability to work effectively with data science teams on technical workflows and tool adoption.

FAQs
1. What does a Systems Analyst do?
A Systems Analyst evaluates business processes and technology systems to identify requirements, resolve problems, and improve how applications support organizational needs. The role often bridges business stakeholders and technical teams by translating operational requirements into practical system solutions.
2. How does a Systems Analyst gather and document requirements?
Systems Analysts gather requirements through stakeholder interviews, process reviews, workshops, existing-system analysis, and documentation reviews. They translate findings into functional requirements, workflows, use cases, process diagrams, and other specifications that guide development or system changes.
3. How does a Systems Analyst analyze existing systems?
The analyst reviews application functionality, data flows, integrations, business processes, and system dependencies to understand how the current environment operates. This analysis helps identify inefficiencies, gaps, risks, technical constraints, and opportunities for improvement.
4. What role does a Systems Analyst play in application integrations?
Systems Analysts help define how applications exchange information and how changes in one system may affect others. They may document APIs, data mappings, integration workflows, business rules, error scenarios, and dependencies to support reliable system-to-system communication.
5. How does a Systems Analyst work with developers?
The analyst provides developers with clear requirements, process flows, business rules, data requirements, and acceptance criteria. Throughout development, they clarify questions, review proposed solutions, validate functionality, and help ensure the delivered system meets the original business need.
6. What tools are commonly used by Systems Analysts?
Systems Analysts may use SQL, Excel, Jira, Confluence, Visio, Lucidchart, diagramming tools, requirements-management platforms, and application monitoring or reporting tools. The specific toolset depends on the organization's technology environment and development methodology.
7. How does a Systems Analyst troubleshoot system issues?
Troubleshooting typically involves reproducing the issue, reviewing system behavior and logs, tracing data flows, examining integrations, and identifying the source of the problem. Analysts collaborate with technical teams to determine root causes and validate fixes before changes are released.
8. What role does SQL play in systems analysis?
SQL can help Systems Analysts investigate application data, validate business rules, identify data inconsistencies, and understand relationships between database entities. It is particularly useful when analyzing system behavior or verifying whether technical changes produce the expected data results.

Resumen del Rol

Como Técnico de Flujo de Materiales (Material Flow Technician), serás responsable de apoyar la ejecución y estabilidad de los procesos internos de suministro, reabastecimiento y manejo de materiales en el piso de producción. Trabajarás en estrecha colaboración con los equipos de Manufactura, Planeación y Almacén para garantizar la disponibilidad de materiales, reducir interrupciones en la línea de producción y mantener un flujo de materiales organizado y confiable.

¿Qué harás?

Monitorear el flujo de materiales para garantizar el suministro oportuno a la producción.

Apoyar la implementación y el control de sistemas Kanban, listas de surtido (pick lists), procesos de reabastecimiento y kits de materiales.

Colaborar con los equipos de Manufactura, Planeación y Almacén para resolver faltantes, desequilibrios y requerimientos urgentes de materiales.

Verificar los niveles de inventario y apoyar la exactitud de los registros, movimientos de materiales y entregas internas.

Participar en actividades de PFEP (Plan para Cada Pieza) y análisis ABC/XYZ para mejorar la clasificación, el reabastecimiento y el manejo de materiales.

Apoyar la definición y el monitoreo de rutas de abastecimiento mediante tugger (tren logístico) y otros métodos de suministro interno.

Dar seguimiento a indicadores clave de desempeño (KPI) relacionados con la disponibilidad de materiales, paros de línea y eficiencia logística.

Contribuir a iniciativas de mejora continua enfocadas en la entrega de materiales, la gestión de inventarios y la estandarización de procesos.

Operar con disciplina, garantizando la seguridad, calidad de datos y cumplimiento de los estándares establecidos.

Mantener una presencia cercana a las operaciones del piso de producción para identificar obstáculos, anticipar riesgos y responder rápidamente a las necesidades de producción.

Utilizar análisis básicos de inventario, reabastecimiento y priorización para tomar decisiones prácticas y sostener las operaciones diarias.

Comunicarte de manera clara con los equipos de Planeación, Almacén y Producción para coordinar acciones y prevenir interrupciones.

Impulsar mejoras continuas mediante la observación, seguimiento de causas raíz y ajustes simples a los procesos que mejoren la estabilidad operativa.

Trabajar como parte de un equipo multifuncional, demostrando colaboración, escucha activa y alineación en las soluciones.

Carrera profesional concluida enfocada a Ingeniería industrial

Job Description Summary
The Department of Art History and Archaeology at the University of Maryland College Park (UMCP) invites applications for an assistant professor of Early Modern European Art History (1300-1800). Topical and geographical specialty is open.

We are particularly interested in scholars with research and teaching interests that complement the Department’s strengths in archaeology and cultural heritage, digital art history, the circulation of objects through trade or conquest, environmental humanities, and histories of race, representation, and colonial power. Candidates are invited to discuss their potential to engage the rich cultural resources of the Washington, D.C.-Maryland-Virginia area in their research and teaching. Successful candidates will demonstrate their readiness to contribute to our undergraduate major and M.A. and Ph.D. programs in Art History and Archaeology through classroom teaching and student mentorship. 

Additional Job Details

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
Applicants must have completed their doctoral degree in Art History or a related field when the term of appointment commences (July 1, 2027). Teaching experience at the college or university level is required.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
We seek candidates whose research, teaching, and service have prepared them to contribute to all the pillars of the College of Arts and Humanities’ Strategic Plan: Transformative Thinking; Boundless Creativity; Expansive Empathy; and Meaningful Futures. Contributions toward those goals and values might include leadership in teaching, mentoring, research, or service toward building an equitable and inclusive scholarly environment and/or increasing access or participation of all individuals equitably and fairly.

REQUIRED APPLICATION MATERIALS (ONLINE):

· 3-4-page letter of application (describing scholarly research agenda and teaching philosophy and experience, including proposed courses)

· curriculum vitae

· writing sample (one article or book/dissertation chapter)

· contact information for three recommenders

Best consideration date: 10/15/2026

Open Until Filled: Yes

Please direct questions to Holly Miller at hmmiller@umd.edu.

The Department of Art History and Archaeology is a community of students and scholars that focuses on visual, material and textual expressions as means to understand culture. We critically engage with the reality of living in a world of images, working across a wide range of histories, perspectives and values. Our students at both the undergraduate and graduate levels learn from internationally recognized faculty experts in the field and engage with leading D.C. area arts institutions. Moreover, all students and faculty benefit from innovative technology and digital approaches through the Michelle Smith Collaboratory for Visual Culture.

About Hy-Vee

At Hy-Vee, we believe the shortest distance between two people is a smile. We're seeking people with a passion for customer service, a willingness to learn, and a commitment to being part of a team that strives to make our customers' lives easier, healthier and happier.

The Role and Why It's Important

As a Barista at Hy-Vee, you'll be the friendly face our customers look forward to seeing every morning. In this role, you'll craft beverages, keep the coffee shop stocked and spotless, and make sure every customer walks away with exactly what they came in for, and a smile to go with it.

If you enjoy connecting with people, love a fast-paced environment, and take pride in doing things well, this could be a great fit for you.

What You'll Do

No two shifts are exactly the same, but here's what you can expect:

Deliver outstanding customer service by greeting customers warmly, learning their names, and going the extra mile to make every visit a positive one

Take customer orders at the counter and over the phone, and assist with finding products and answering questions

Prepare and replenish coffee shop products as needed throughout your shift

Monitor product freshness and appearance and follow or develop a production list to stay ahead of daily needs

Handle food safely and keep the work area clean, neat, and up to department standards at all times

Check in product, put product away, and review invoices as needed

Run the department register and process payments where applicable

Remove trash promptly and maintain a tidy department

Work alongside your teammates to ensure a smooth, positive experience for every customer

Maintain compliance with Hy-Vee's dress code, hygiene standards, and all company policies

Assist in other store areas and take on special projects as needed

Your Skills

You don't need prior experience for this role! We'll happily train and support you as you grow. To be successful, you'll need to be able to:

Follow written and verbal instructions with confidence

Use basic math skills for simple addition, subtraction, counting, and recording

Communicate clearly with customers and teammates in a friendly, helpful way

Stay organized and keep up with the pace of a busy coffee shop environment

Less than a high school diploma or equivalent accepted; up to six months of similar or related experience preferred

Accountable and Reports to: Store Director, Store Manager, Assistant Managers of Store Operations, Perishables, and Health Wellness Home, Food Service Director, and Coffee Shop Department Manager

Education and Experience

Less than a high school diploma or equivalent experience accepted

Up to six months of similar or related work experience preferred

Physical Requirements

Frequently stand and walk throughout a shift in sales, food service, or delivery areas

Where applicable to the role: ability to safely use sharp knives and blades for food preparation

Where applicable to the role: exposure to heat- and burn-related hazards associated with cooking, baking, or grilling equipment

Where applicable to the role: ability to operate a delivery vehicle in accordance with applicable DOT standards

Perform repetitive standing, walking, reaching, and bending associated with order fulfillment, POS transactions, and cleaning/sanitation duties

Working Environment

This role is performed in a store coffee shop environment with significant pressure to meet deadlines and manage multiple priorities throughout your shift. You may encounter exposure to noise, equipment movement hazards, cleaning chemicals or solvents, and possible electrical shock and temperature extremes. Safety is always a priority, and training is provided to help ensure a safe and supportive work environment.

Are you ready to smile, apply today.

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience

Global supply chains still rely on slow, manual processes—email, spreadsheets, and fragmented data. The economy moves fast but supply chains don't, creating an inefficiency that affects the $13T of goods shipped annually and is one of the largest untapped opportunities in modern enterprise.

Agentforce Operations is reimagining the supply chain with an AI-powered platform for designing, automating, and running end-to-end business processes, with seamless collaboration through familiar channels like email. For Salesforce, this represents a massive growth opportunity in the back office, with innovations that flow into the front office. Customers are clamoring for more, rapidly expanding their use cases as we enter an exhilarating growth phase. As one user put it: "I've been waiting for this for 20 years."

The Teams

Agentforce Operations & Missionforce Team

As a Site Reliability Engineer for Missionforce Operations, you will be a senior technical contributor who helps shape the infrastructure, process automation and engineering practices behind the product. You will partner closely with product engineers, sector experts, and forward-deployed engineers to deliver the most reliable systems for mission-critical public-sector workflows.

Missionforce Operations is Agentforce Operations’ public-sector counterpart: rebuilt from the ground up to bring core capabilities to some of the world’s most sensitive operating environments. In this role, you will design and ship infrastructure, automation, and cost-efficient platform capabilities that enable customers to run Missionforce Operations reliably and securely in customer-owned, isolated public-cloud environments, where requirements for trust, security, and data classification are uncompromising.

Super Agent Team

As a Site Reliability Engineer for the Agentforce Operations Super Agent team, your mandate will be to radically optimize the scalability, resilience, and performance of our product and platform across the entire stack to help usher in this next phase of growth. The ideal candidate would be able to develop a deep technical understanding of our architecture and then deliver the end-to-end implementation of optimizations that would enable us to achieve greater scalability while simultaneously improving our reliability. Agentforce Operations manages complex, infinitely configurable states with equally complex state transitions and interfaces to teams across the organization. That means you'd be tackling a wide array of challenges that would include optimization of our existing data model, streamlining of our asynchronous operations patterns, profiling and rightsizing our infrastructure, and developing both the tools and observability to run experiments and empirically validate results.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Agentforce Operations & Missionforce Team
 

Scaling & Reliability: Own the reliability roadmap for major product areas, evolving startup-speed architectures into highly available, globally scalable systems for mission-critical customer-operated cloud environments.

Collaborative Leadership: Partner with engineers to refine our infrastructure strategy, contributing senior-level perspectives on system design, capacity planning, bottleneck identification, and security.

Infrastructure as Code: Define, maintain and evolve our tools for deployments, focusing on making deployments as “push-button” and robust as possible.

AI Operations (AIOps): Support the scaling and deployment of our AI/ML infrastructure, ensuring the compute, deployment and platform capabilities required to run AI features reliably and cost-effectively.

Production Excellence: Design and build the internal systems and processes for testing and releasing the product, along with the tooling and automation that enable customers and partners to deploy, upgrade, diagnose, and run Missionforce Operations successfully with minimal direct engineering involvement.

Security Engineering: Design, review, and strengthen identity and access controls, networking, workload isolation, secret management, deployment security, and policy enforcement to ensure the product is secure by default.

AI-First Workflow: Lean into the future of engineering by using AI tools to automate routine operational tasks and accelerate infrastructure delivery.

Super Agent
 

Diagnose and prioritize architectural problems across our distributed backend systems, contributing technical perspective to help the team invest in the right foundational work at the right time

Design and implement solutions to hard system problems including application performance optimization, infrastructure management, and data model improvements. 

Raise and maintain our engineering quality bar through pragmatic standards, guardrails, and team practices that prevent regressions and keep our product healthy and performant. 

Collaborate with peers across customer, product, and engineering to deeply understand customer needs, make pragmatic tradeoffs that maximize impact, and align on engineering reality

Mentor engineers as a senior peer and force multiplier, sharing expertise across backend architecture and system design while helping shape stronger engineering judgment, more effective collaboration, and a higher-performing team

You're Our Person If...
 

Agentforce Operations & Missionforce Team

Proven Production Experience: Experience supporting mission-critical production systems and helping high-growth products navigate the technical debt and architectural changes required to scale reliably.

Technical Breadth: Strong proficiency in Kubernetes, Terraform/OpenTofu, and AWS/GCP/Azure.

Coding Mastery: Ability to write and review production-level code in Golang, TypeScript, or Python—you view automation as a software engineering problem.

Systems Expert: Deep understanding of distributed systems, including how to debug complex interactions between microservices, databases, and AI agents.

Low-Ego Collaboration: Experience working within a senior team of Principal engineers, capable of both leading specific initiatives and supporting the broader group’s technical vision.

Mentorship Mindset: Enthusiasm for learning and growing as an engineer, and for helping your peers do the same.

Designing, developing, and maintaining web applications using ASP.NET MVC, WCF, and Web API, ensuring high performance, scalability, and reliability across all deliverables.
Building and integrating RESTful and SOAP-based web services, working with XML and JSON data formats to connect systems and deliver seamless user experiences.
Writing clean, maintainable, and efficient code using C# and object-oriented programming principles, contributing to code reviews and best practices across the team.
Developing interactive and responsive front-end features using jQuery, collaborating closely with UI/UX teams to deliver engaging user interfaces.
Managing source code, branching strategies, and version control workflows using Git, ensuring code quality and collaboration standards are consistently upheld.

Proven ability to design and consume Web Services (SOAP, REST), working with XML and JSON, with solid knowledge of WCF architecture and integration patterns.
Experience working in Agile/Scrum environments, with the ability to collaborate effectively within cross-functional teams, contribute to sprint ceremonies, and deliver iteratively.
Working knowledge of Git for source control, including branching, merging, and pull request workflows in a collaborative development environment.
Basic knowledge of SQL or Oracle PL/SQL, with the ability to write and understand queries to support application data needs.

Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. • Early in your career, you earned a reputation for solving the toughest problems others couldn’t crack. As your career advanced, so did the complexity of the challenges you tackled. You value collaborating with SRE, Engineering, and Infrastructure teams to ensure architectures are robust, systems are finely tuned, and your teams’ code is optimized for its environment.
• Aware that your software serves as critical financial infrastructure for multiple nation-states, you balance hands-on leadership with a focus on ensuring SDLC and governance processes are both effective and responsible.

Whether fostering inclusive ideation sessions where every voice is respected or staying in the trenches during production crises to resolve last-minute issues, you set a personal standard that defines the team’s culture.

Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;

Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;

Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and

Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

Responsibilities may include: 

Support design development and integration of EOIR sensor subsystems and components to meet platform mission objectives

Development, analysis, maturation and implementation translating customer requirements into hardware and software specifications

Modeling/Developing / analyzing sensor performance, predicting performance as installed on an airborne platform

Solicit input from various stakeholders, synthesize data, and communicate results 

Ensure performance capabilities of new systems traded against cost and mission requirements and assess operational effectiveness of existing and emerging systems and capabilities in representative operational environments.

Ability to build and test hardware prototypes in a laboratory environment

Perform characterization of EOIR subsystems and component level parts

 

Basic Qualifications:

Demonstrated experience with sensor development, IR payloads, fiber optics

Background in EO/IR and laser technology and system design for airborne or space platforms

Experience with EO/IR sensor component design and performance analysis 

Experience in the modeling of EO/IR systems to assess performance

Knowledge of system engineering design methods, including requirements analysis and flow-down, specification derivation and interface control documentation

Preferred Qualifications:

Strong desire to learn, take initiative and contribute in a team-oriented environment

Demonstrated mathematical problem-solving ability and data analysis experience

Demonstrated interpersonal communication, presentation skills, verbal and written communication skills

Work experience with one of the following areas related to EOIR systems: lasers, LiDAR, Sensing, surveillance, reconnaissance, electronic protection, ID, or adaptive technique

Customer focus and collaboration skills

Demonstrated team leadership experience

An understanding of the physical limitations to implementing complex algorithms in real hardware

Experience working with free-space optics and characterizing optical/laser systems 

Use of optical metrology to measure parameters such as laser power, wavelength, pulse width, divergence and beam quality

About SpotOn

We’re not just building restaurant tech, we’re giving independent restaurants the tools to compete and win. From our award-winning point-of-sale to AI-powered profit tools, everything we do helps operators boost profit, work smarter, and keep their best people. And every solution is backed by real humans who actually give a sh*t about helping restaurants succeed.

 - Named the #1 Restaurant POS by G2 (Summer 2026), based on ratings from real users

We move fast, care hard, and fight for independent restaurant operators to do what they love, and love doing it. If you’re looking to make an impact with heart and hustle, SpotOn is the place for you.

Our Financial Services group is looking for a Software Implementation & Support Specialist to join our Implementation team! This role will focus on DayCheck, SpotOn’s earned wage access solution designed to give restaurant employees access to their hard-earned tips once they’re approved—improving financial flexibility for employees and streamlining operations for restaurants.

This role will involve implementing DayCheck for new merchants and supporting the growth of the product. Because DayCheck integrates directly with our labor management system (Teamwork), you’ll also become an expert in Teamwork’s tools and data flows. While the core focus is implementation, your work will also equip you to assist with escalated support cases requiring advanced troubleshooting. As DayCheck evolves to support new features and integrations, your scope will grow with it.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

 - Implementation Coordination: Lead the setup and configuration of new DayCheck accounts, coordinating across teams and partners to ensure merchants and employees have a smooth experience regardless of which SpotOn tools or services they’re adopting

 - Quality Assurance: Validate account setup by running tip flow checks and pre-launch QA steps

 - Training & Enablement: Train merchants and internal teams on how DayCheck works, including system behavior, reporting logic, and key DayCheck workflows.

 - Account Monitoring: Oversee new merchant launches through their first few weeks, including working alongside Teamwork specialists to verify initial payroll setup and reconciliation. Assist with handoff to Support and Customer Success once stable.

 - Product Knowledge: Become an expert in DayCheck and Teamwork’s integration logic, with the ability to understand and explain how data flows from shifts and tips to payouts and merchant settlements.

 - Support Escalation: Handle advanced support requests from frontline teams, especially those related to implementation configurations, money movement, integrations, or reconciliation across systems.

 - Pipeline Management: Monitor new activation cases, document progress, track implementation steps, and ensure all account data is properly recorded in SpotOn’s systems

 - Cross-Team Collaboration: Work closely with global (especially U.S.- and India-based) teammates in Implementation, Product, Engineering, Support, and Customer Success.

 - Growth Support: Contribute to tooling improvements, process documentation, and feedback loops that inform product, process, and implementation improvements




MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of experience in product implementation, technical onboarding, or customer support roles

 - Strong problem-solving skills and comfort working with multiple systems and internal tools.

 - Proven ability to convey complex step-by-step instructions in layman's terms

 - Experience with restaurant operations, Point-of-Sale (POS) systems, payroll platforms, earned wage access tools, or labor management platforms is a plus.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication and clear documentation habits.

 - Demonstrates excellent organizational skills

 - Keen attention to detail

 - Solution-oriented

 - Strong customer empathy, and driven to see clients and team members succeed.

 - Ability to maintain professionalism in a client-facing role.

 - Ability to think through edge cases and troubleshoot across integrated systems using strong analytical and critical problem-solving skills

 - Comfortable working in a collaborative team environment and independently driving tasks forward.

 - Ability to effectively manage multiple projects simultaneously

EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS

 - High School Diploma

 - Bachelor’s Degree preferred

JOB AND WORKING CONDITIONS

 - The majority of work time will be spent on a computer using Zoom, Slack, and other internal tools.

 - Remote-first role with occasional in-person team sessions if applicable.

 - Must be able to work independently and maintain reliable internet access in a secure and distraction-free environment.

 - Working Hours: 5:00 PM–2:00 AM IST


BENEFITS

At SpotOn, we prioritize people above all else. While we're recognized for our innovative technology solutions, it's our people who drive our success. That’s why we offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support your well-being and growth:

 - Medical Insurance with coverage up to INR 8,00,000 for the employee and their family

The Arctic Wolf security operations platform ingests and processes upwards of 600 billion events a day from a wide variety of on-premise devices and

cloud platforms. The security pipeline is a distributed system of loosely-coupled microservices that constitute our Realtime analysis and threat detection

systems. These services distil the incoming events into actionable intelligence that our Concierge Security Teams use to protect customers.

We are looking for experienced quality engineers to join our pack and work with us to build and expand the capabilities of our testing platform.

Create and extend software frameworks and tools to run, monitor, and report on automated tests. Have experience building and maintaining Automation frameworks and CI/CD pipeline.

Review testing strategies, approaches, and test plans and provide insight to development teams.

Architect, design and build software to automate a variety of testing methods (e.g. API validation, performance/load testing, fuzzing, etc.)

Develop and maintain test frameworks for GenAI-based and AI/ML applications, including model validation, LLM prompt-response consistency,

hallucination detection, and regression testing for AI inference APIs.

Implement evaluation pipelines to test LLM accuracy, latency, bias, toxicity, and reliability.

Work as part of a team of highly skilled software professionals.

Continuously learn and expand your technical horizons

Our Technology Stack: Python , Selenium, Playwright, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS (Bedrock, Lambda, SQS, S3, etc.), LangChain, LLM evaluation frameworks (e.g., Ragas), OpenAPI, Postgres, Linux.

Have 8+ years of experience shipping quality software

Love driving high software quality

Have experience deploying services on cloud computing platforms (e.g, AWS, Azure, GCP)

Are an expert using common tools for executing functional, load and fuzz testing (e.g. Locust, CATS)

Job Description
 

At Gilead our pursuit of a healthier world for all people has yielded a cure for hepatitis C, revolutionary improvements in HIV treatment and prevention as well as advancements in therapies for viral and inflammatory diseases and certain cancers. 

 

We set and achieve bold ambitions in our fight against the world’s most devastating diseases, united in our commitment to confronting the largest public health challenges of our day and improving the lives of patients for generations to come.  As a Senior Medical Science Liaison at Gilead you will be part of the Breast team of Medical Science Liaisons reporting to a regional Field Director. The MSL will disseminate clinical information about Gilead’s innovative oncology products to key opinion leaders, academic institutions, community group practices, healthcare professionals (including allied healthcare members), and professional organizations. 

**The geography is South Texas Region**

Responsibilities: 

Responds to clinical inquiries regarding marketed or developmental Gilead products.

Develops and presents complex scientific and clinical data for these products.

Identifies and develops regional and national opinion leaders to support Gilead products and trains Gilead approved speakers through personal contacts and on-site visits.

Establishes strong relationships with opinion leaders, clinical investigators and providers at academic and non-academic settings.

Provides sales force with training at national and regional levels.

Works on Gilead Phase IV program that includes collaboration with investigators and internal Gilead personnel.

Selects sites for both Phase IV and other clinical trials.

Anticipates complex obstacles and difficulties that may arise in the field and resolves them in a collaborative manner.

The Senior MSL works collaboratively with Gilead personnel in Sales, Marketing, Clinical Research, Global Safety and Medical Communication.

Others both from within and outside Gilead seek the Senior MSL out for advice and collaboration on complex issues and resolution of complex problems.

Utilizes scientific resources to deliver impactful presentations in a variety of different settings.

The Senior MSL travels to appointments, meetings and conferences on a frequent and regular basis, occasionally with short notice.

Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills are required.

The Senior MSL must be fully cognizant of all relevant complex scientific data. Must also be cognizant of complex regulatory requirements for field-based personnel.

Must be committed to continuing education to maintain knowledge base.

Others both from within and outside Gilead seek the Senior MSL out for advice and collaboration.

Anticipates complex obstacles and difficulties that may arise in the field and acts upon these to resolve them in a collaborative manner.

Must have the ability to work as a member of several teams that may overlap such as national MS team, regional sales team, national accounts, and others.

Utilizes scientific resources for impactful presentations in a variety of different settings.

Advanced degree (i.e. MD, DO, PharmD, PhD, NP/PA) required or may have a BS in pharmacy or BS/MS nursing with varying levels of clinical and/or industry experience.

BA/BS and 10+ years of experience OR

MA/MS and 8+ years of experience OR

PhD/ PharmD/ MD/ DO/ NP/PA and 5+ years of experience

Relevant experience must include at least 5 yrs clinical practice experience.

Demonstrated ability to work independently

Well-developed experience in preparing and delivering presentations is required. 

Experience in the management or investigation of clinical trials is required.

Clinical patient contact experience is required.

Preferred:

Clinical practice/industry experience within therapeutic area of interest desirable.

Advanced degree is strongly preferred

2027 Systems Engineering Apprentice - Level 6 Applied Professional Engineering Degree Apprenticeship

 

Start Date: 6 September 2027

Salary: £24,000 per annum

Employee type: Permanent

Location: Cheadle

Working Schedule: Monday – Friday, 37 hours a week (8 hours Monday – Thursday, 5 hours Friday)

 

Turn your curiosity into a career. If you're passionate about engineering, eager to learn, and looking for a degree apprenticeship that combines academic study with exciting on-the-job experience, we'd love to hear from you.

 

Benefits of the programme:

Earn a salary while studying for your degree

Gain hands-on experience in a real engineering environment

Receive job-specific training and development

Achieve a recognised engineering qualification

Secure a permanent role from the start of your apprenticeship

Have your university tuition fees fully paid

 

About the Role

 

As a Systems Engineering Apprentice, you will develop the technical knowledge, practical skills and professional behaviours needed to become a confident and capable engineer.

Working as part of our Systems Engineering team, you will support the delivery of systems and equipment solutions, ensuring projects are completed on time and within budget.

 

Your responsibilities may include:

 

Supporting systems requirements and design activities

Contributing to project reviews

Participating in system testing and validation activities

Assisting with engineering investigations and problem solving

Visiting customer sites, platforms and installations to support surveys, trials and system deployment where required

Working with experienced engineers on live projects

 

What You Will Learn

 

Throughout the apprenticeship, you will gain experience and knowledge in:

 

Professional engineering behaviours and industry best practice

Understanding and working with complex engineering systems

Different engineering roles and activities across live projects

The Systems Engineering Lifecycle and key engineering processes

Requirements capture, requirements management and system design techniques

Systems engineering tools and methods

Testing, integration, verification, validation and qualification (IVVQ) activities

Structured and methodical approaches to problem solving and investigation

 

 

Degree Apprenticeship Programme

 

You will study towards the BEng Applied Professional Engineering Degree Apprenticeship with The University of Warwick, following the Product Design and Development Engineer pathway.

 

The programme is delivered through a blended learning approach, combining:

 

On-campus teaching (approximately 12 blocks of 3 days)

Virtual coaching sessions

Online learning resources

 

Programme structure:

 

This is a broad programme, designed to provide a strong multi-disciplinary engineering foundation prior to moving onto a more specialist pathway.

 

Years 1 and 2

 

Mechanical Engineering

Electrical and Electronic Engineering

Materials and Design

Computational skills

 

Years 3 and 4

 

Progress onto the Design and Development Engineer specialist pathway

Work based project

 

Throughout the four-year programme, you will combine university study with practical workplace experience, developing both academic knowledge and professional engineering skills. Aligned to the IET accreditation requirements, this degree will support those looking to become a Chartered Engineer in future.

 

Entry Requirements

 

To apply, you will need:

 

A Levels

Minimum 112 UCAS Tariff points at A Level, including a grade B in Maths and at least one further STEM or engineering subject

 

 GCSEs

Minimum of five GCSEs at Grade 4/C or above

Must include:

English Language

Mathematics

Additional STEM subject

 

Please note that applicants who already hold a relevant degree will not be eligible for this programme.

 

Benefits

 

·         Competitive salary of £24,000 per annum

·         Performance-related pay uplifts

·         Holiday entitlement of 201 hours a year (plus a company day and bank holidays)

·         Contributory Company Pension

·         Health Care Cash Plan

·         Hybrid/flexible working options

·         Employee assistance programme

·         Learning and development support

·         Employee discounts and wellbeing initiatives

·         Life Cover

·         80 Hours Volunteering per year (first two years)

 

 

Thales Apprentice Recruitment Process

 

1.      Apply Online - submit your application online to register your interest.  You only need to register for one role as you will have the opportunity to apply for additional roles at the full application stage.

 

2.      Upload Your CV

 

3.      Check your emails for the invitation to apply – this will come from recruiting@jobalerts.thalesgroup.com

 

4.      Complete Your Application – follow the link provided in the email to complete your application.  You can apply for one primary role and up to 3 additional roles.

5.      Complete Online Tests - undertake the online assessments designed to evaluate your  suitability for the role.

 

6.      Virtual Assessment Centre - candidates who progress from the online assessment stage will attend a virtual assessment centre, which will include group exercises, and competency-based interviews.

7.      Job Offer – successful candidates who perform well throughout the recruitment process will receive a job offer from Thales.

For further information about our Future Talent recruitment process, including hints and tips, or to connect with a member of the Future Talent Team, a Graduate, or an Apprentice, please visit Thales Future Talent - Connectr.

 

 

Please note, assessment centres for shortlisted candidates will be held between February - May 2027.  Induction week for all Graduate and Apprentices will take place from Monday 6 September - Friday 10 September 2027.

 

Closing date: Our applications will close at 11.59pm on Wednesday 17 February 2027, this is the only time we will be accepting applications this year. Please note, we will be in contact by the end of February 2027 with details of next steps.

To be considered for this position, you must have the permanent right to work in the UK and be able to successfully complete and maintain UK Government security checks, including Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) screening and Security Clearance (SC), which is a government background check, before starting employment.

KBR, as part of the Linewide Alliance, is proud to be awarded the Suburban Rail Loop (SRL) East Linewide Alliance contract. SRL is a city-shaping infrastructure project that will transform how people live and move around Melbourne. The 90km orbital rail line will connect every major train line, link key precincts, and support vibrant communities. SRL East, the first stage, will deliver 26km of twin underground tunnels and six new stations between Cheltenham and Box Hill, enabling 70,000 new homes near public transport, jobs, schools, and services. It will create diverse, accessible communities shaped by local input, with upgraded open space, bike paths, and essential infrastructure. 

The Alliance, comprising John Holland, Alstom, RATP DEC, WSP, and KBR, will deliver The Linewide package of works, which includes tunnel fit-outs, rolling stock, and construction of depot and maintenance facilities. This package is critical to safe, efficient train operations and long-term performance across SRL East. 

KBR, alongside WSP as Designer Non-Owner Participant, is leading comprehensive design services and contributing to alliance management. Our infrastructure design scope includes track, overhead line equipment, drainage and overland flow, civil works, tunnel portals, building structures and services, HV and LV power systems, cable containment, systems integration and safety assurance, ensuring seamless delivery across the corridor. 

 

The Opportunity: 

KBR have an exciting opportunity for a Fire Designer to join our Buildings team in Melbourne. Flexible work arrangements and work/life balance. 

National career pathways and exposure to multidisciplinary teams. 

 

Join a team where people matter, your expertise is respected, and your work directly shapes critical Australian infrastructure.

Our KBR Values - We Value Our People, We Deliver, We Are People of Integrity, We Empower, We Are a Team of Teams - embody our people centric organisation. 

Our culture, and our genuine focus on our people is a major factor in our success and we want you to be part of our journey.

Join a fast-paced Phantom Works program as a Mid-Level or Senior Design and Analysis Engineer in Berkeley, MO. This program is responsible for integrating complex tactical system-of-systems mission capabilities across sensors, mission management, communications, networks, and weapons/effector interfaces. This role focuses on end-to-end integration of multiple subsystems and external sources into a cohesive tactical mission capability that performs reliably in real operational environments.

You will help define, architect, and verify mission solutions that span payloads, distributed sensors, datalinks, and mission management functions. The role includes requirements definition, SysML/MBSE-based architecture modeling, system integration, verification, and stakeholder communication across engineering disciplines and program stakeholders.

Position Responsibilities:

Define and manage system requirements and interfaces for system-of-systems mission integration across sensors, mission management functions, communications, and weapons/payload interfaces.

Architect and document end-to-end mission system integrations, including system interdependencies, data flows, timing budgets, synchronization, and operational constraints.

Develop and maintain SysML/MBSE artifacts that describe system architecture, functional decomposition, interface behavior, requirement traceability, and verification mapping.

Support integration of onboard and offboard systems, including distributed sensors, datalinks, external mission services, and partner-provided capabilities.

Develop and evaluate mission system logic related to sensor integration, track management, mission planning, state awareness, decision support, and effect coordination.

Analyze failure modes, sensitivity, and robustness; define fault detection, degradation, and recovery behaviors for mission-critical, multi-system architectures.

Produce concise technical documentation supporting design decisions, model assumptions, verification results, integration artifacts, and compliance/safety evidence.

Communicate technical tradeoffs, risks, and recommended paths forward to leadership, customers, and cross-functional partners.

Own assigned capabilities end-to-end, from requirements through architecture modeling, prototype, integration, verification, optimization, deployment, and sustainment.

Mentor junior engineers and contribute to reusable patterns, standards, and integration best practices.

Support demonstrations, technical reviews, and program execution as a key contributor to the team.

Bachelor of Science degree in Engineering (with a focus in Electrical, Mechanical or Aeronautical), Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry or non-US equivalent qualifications directly related to the work statement

Experience applying SysML and MBSE to system-of-systems, tactical mission systems, embedded systems, or platform integration.

Demonstrated experience with MBSE and SysML, including creating or maintaining system architecture models, requirements relationships, and behavioral definitions.

Experience integrating or characterizing mission systems on tactical platforms.

Familiarity with embedded deployment, real-time scheduling, and latency analysis.

Knowledge of mission data standards, interface management, or subsystem interoperability practices.

Prior experience supporting technical reviews, customer demonstrations, or operational assessments.

MSOSA experience is preferred, if applicable to the team’s MBSE tooling/processes.

Job Description

The Role

Join an enthusiastic and cutting-edge team here at General Motors in the Automated Driving Performance HIL team!  ADAS is a rapidly developing domain, deploying multiple new features, subsystems and sensing systems to the vehicle, and a key part of GM’s Zero Crashes, Zero Emissions, Zero Congestion vision.  This is a great opportunity to join our team as an Automated Driving Performance HIL Infrastructure Engineer!

Our group is responsible for a simulation toolchain used to evaluate the vehicle level performance of ADAS control features. The toolchain is anchored in a realistic 3D virtual environment, and represents sensors, physical vehicle systems, and control systems utilizing a variety of hardware (HiL) configurations running in real-time.

You’ll partner with software, capability, and program execution teams to move their testing from prototype vehicles to the virtual domain, working on features such as automatic emergency braking, lane keeping assist, adaptive cruise control, SuperCruise lane centering and more.

This role involves simulation capability and toolchain development as well as some program execution support as related to ensuring the team delivers results on time and with quality.

What You'll Do

Create & integrate models, software and hardware into our simulation infrastructure

These can include Simulink models to represent consumed serial data, 3d virtual road network and traffic scenarios, Carsim, dSPACE ASM & other plant models to represent the vehicle’s physical systems, and sensor models used by the ADAS controller

Manage hardware-in-the-loop simulators (dSPACE, etc.) to support customers’ automated driving control code development and validation objectives

Partner with the ADAS community to identify new opportunities to utilize simulation, decreasing reliance on physical test properties

Advance the development of the core co-simulation infrastructure.  Scout new technology & methods for opportunities to improve system capability, efficiency and robustness

Actively foster a collaborative and productive work environment

Your Skills & Abilities

Experience with any of the following:

Model, software, or hardware in the loop control system simulation experience, especially with dSPACE HiL and Simulink

Vehicle controls system experience (ADAS, chassis controls, powertrain controls, etc.), in algorithm development or calibration.  Including expertise with CAN or automotive ethernet.

Active safety, automated driving, or autonomous vehicle related experience – in software development, calibration, design/release, testing, or validation.

Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering or other related engineering degree

5yrs of experience with 3yrs of experience in HIL simulation and test execution

Excellent interpersonal skills to work in a highly collaborative, diverse, multi-functional team and with a broad customer base

High level of analytical ability where problems are unusual, difficult and ambiguous

What Will Give You A Competitive Edge

Virtual environment and sensor modeling software experience- such as dSpace ASM/Aurelion, CarSim, Hexagon Virtual Test Drive (VTD), CARLA, Carmaker, Prescan, SCANeR, rFactor, Forum8, or Mathworks Automated Driving System Toolbox

Experience with SOME/IP.

Experience with Software Defined Vehicle (SDV).

Background with Python scripting for test automation applications

Vehicle dynamics / brakes / steering / chassis controls experience, especially in controls simulation

Experience with automotive control system instrumentation, such as INCA or ETAS

Data analytics experience

Autodesk 3ds Max, Unity, Unreal, or other computer graphics / visual effects experience

Full motion or static driving simulator experience

Master of Science degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering or other related engineering degree

5yrs experience in HIL simulation and test execution

Experience with Vector tools in HIL simulation and test execution.

Reports to: Creative Lead
Location: Remote (U.S. or Canada); West Coast preferred or PST hours required.



About the role

NETGEAR is building an in-house creative team to own campaign, web, and social work end to end. The team is small on purpose: a Creative Lead, a UI Designer, a Graphic Designer, and a copywriter.

This work supports the Consumer-facing side of NETGEAR. You will be the main person responsible for execution and production across what the team makes: web assets, social, paid ads, campaign work, email templates, retail signage, and event booth graphics. In a given month you might move from a paid social set to a booth graphic to a product landing page.

Everything runs to established NETGEAR brand guidelines. The craft is in making distinctive work within those rules rather than around them.

You will also work with the Creative Lead on campaign concepts and help shape where the brand goes next. We are looking for someone who brings ideas, not only someone who executes them well.

What you will do

 - Design assets across web, social, paid ads, email templates, campaign work, retail signage, event graphics, and sales collateral, working from briefs and alongside the UI Designer and Creative Lead.

 - Contribute creative ideas. Bring concepts into campaign discussions with the Creative Lead, and propose directions of your own.

 - Adapt campaign concepts into full asset sets across formats, sizes, and channels.

 - Work to NETGEAR brand guidelines across everything you produce, applying them consistently and helping extend the system as new needs come up.

 - Prepare and hand off production-ready files for both screen and print.

 - Use AI tools as a working part of your process, for ideation, iteration, and production. Fluency is welcome, but a genuine interest in the tools and a willingness to build them into how you work matters more. What we do expect is the judgment to recognize when AI output falls short of the standard required and needs to be reworked by hand.

 - Collaborate directly with project stakeholders across marketing, product, and web, and incorporate their feedback into revisions.

 - Work closely with our Sr. Integrated Marketing Manager, who is responsible for global campaigns, so that what you produce fits the wider campaign plan.

What we are looking for

 - 4+ years of professional graphic design experience, ideally in-house or brand-side. Consumer tech, DTC, or ecommerce experience is a strong plus.

 - A portfolio showing volume and range, not just showpiece work. We want to see campaign systems, social sets, and web assets, and hear what the constraints were.

 - Strong fluency in Figma. Most of our digital assets are designed there, so this is the tool you will spend most of your time in. Solid Adobe Creative Cloud skills alongside it.

 - Strong interest in AI, backed by practical experience using it in a design workflow. You should be following how the tools are developing, testing new ones as they appear rather than reading about them, and bringing back what actually works. 

 - A sharp eye for detail. Spacing, alignment, typography, and colour handled precisely, and errors caught before they reach a stakeholder or a printer.

 - Ideas of your own. We want to see concept thinking in your portfolio, not only well-executed versions of someone else’s direction.

 - Comfortable working to an existing brand system rather than reinventing one per project.

 - A positive, curious attitude and a real appetite for learning. We support training on new tools, AI in particular.

 - Reliable under a queue. You can hold several projects at different stages and keep the status visible without being chased.

Nice to have

 - Video and motion. This is a direction we want to push, and the role may grow toward it over time, but we are hiring a designer, not a videographer. Any motion or editing experience is a real benefit, and familiarity with AI video and editing tools is especially so.

 - Print production experience: bleed, colour profiles, and preparing files to a printer’s spec. Useful from day one, but we can teach it if the rest is there.

 - Experience working alongside a design system or component library.

How we work

Fully remote, PST hours. The team works from a shared project board in monday.com http://monday.com and in short review cycles rather than long agency-style handoffs. You will have direct access to the Creative Lead and to stakeholders, and you are expected to use it.

Tooling is provided, including Figma, Adobe Creative Cloud, and a Magnific seat, so you are not funding your own AI tools. We support training on new tools, particularly AI.

 

Company Statement/Values:  

At NETGEAR, we are on a mission to unleash the full potential of connectivity with intelligent solutions that delight and protect. We turn ideas into innovative networking products that connect people, power businesses, and advance the way we live.  

We're a performance-driven, talented and connected team that's committed to delivering world-class products for our customers. As a company, we value our employees as the most essential building blocks of our success. And as teammates, we commit to taking our work to the Next Gear by living our values: we Dare to Transform the future, Connect and Delight our customers, Communicate Courageously with each other and collaborate to Win It Together. You’ll find our values woven through our processes, present in our decisions, and celebrated throughout our culture. 

We strive to attract top talent and create a great workplace where people feel engaged, inspired, challenged, proud and respected. If you are creative, forward-thinking, passionate about technology and are looking for a rewarding career to make an impact, then you've got what it takes to succeed at NETGEAR. Join our network and help us shape the future of connectivity. 



NETGEAR hires based on merit. All qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

A Property Officer is typically responsible for supporting the effective management, maintenance, and administration of real estate assets on behalf of an organization, property owner, or government agency. While specific duties can vary by employer and sector (commercial, residential, public, or institutional), a general job description includes the following:

Key Responsibilities:

Property Inspections: Conduct routine inspections of buildings and grounds to assess condition, identify maintenance issues, and ensure compliance with safety and regulatory standards.

Lease Administration Support: Assist in managing lease documentation, tracking key dates (e.g., renewals, expirations), and coordinating with tenants or landlords as needed.

Vendor Coordination: Liaise with contractors, service providers, and maintenance teams to schedule and oversee repairs, cleaning, security, and other property services.

Compliance & Reporting: Ensure properties adhere to local building codes, health and safety regulations, and accessibility requirements; prepare inspection reports and maintenance logs.

Tenant Liaison: Serve as a point of contact for tenant inquiries, complaints, or requests related to building operations.

Budget & Cost Tracking: Monitor operational expenses, process invoices, and assist in preparing budget forecasts for property-related costs.

Documentation Management: Maintain accurate records of property files, including leases, permits, insurance certificates, and maintenance histories.

Asset Protection: Implement measures to safeguard property assets, reduce risks, and respond to emergencies (e.g., floods, power outages, security incidents).

Diploma or degree in property management, real estate, facilities management, business administration, or a related field (requirements vary by employer).

Experience in property management, facilities coordination, or administrative support within real estate.

Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.

Proficiency in property management software (e.g., Yardi, MRI) and Microsoft Office Suite.

On-site –Hong Kong, SAR, China

Cleveland-Cliffs is seeking an Internal Auditor at our Burns Harbor, Indiana location. This role plans and executes audits and compliance activities, helping the business manage strategic risks, improve or develop efficient and effective business processes, and identify and communicate best practices to foster appropriate control levels for business and financial risks.

Summary of Responsibilities

Work with Internal Audit management to determine the direction and scope of audits and assist in the preparation of planning memorandums and audit programs.

Conduct audits, including the detailed planning of each audit and agreeing the audit objectives and scope with management.

Evaluate and document process, system and control effectiveness through the application of accounting, auditing and business knowledge; collect, analyze, and document information to support audit results.

Assist with SOX scoping, planning and administration, including maintenance of process documentation, planning memos, risk and control matrices and testing plans.

Execute testing of key SOX controls in conjunction with the annual test plan. 

Assess the overall significance of the control deficiencies identified during the audit.  Provide perspective for evaluating the audit deficiencies against evolving industry best practices.

Assist in the preparation and presentation of audit results and strive to improve their communication to appropriate management levels to maximize value of audit services.

Identify and facilitate resolution of issues that may inhibit audit team's performance and resolve outstanding questions/issues related to the audit.

Identify constructive and value-added solutions to address issues identified.  Recommend operation improvements which ensure that proper controls are exercised over all aspects of the business and that company assets are conserved, protected and accurately presented.

Monitor status of action plans arising from audits.

Maintain the confidentiality of audit findings and Company proprietary information.

Develop and maintain effective working relationships with Internal Audit’s stakeholders.

Conduct work in accordance with the Standards for the Professional Practice of Internal Auditing and Code of Ethics promulgated by the Institute of Internal Auditors.

Other duties as assigned

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.

Excellent written and oral communication skills, strong organizational and analytical skills

Ability to maintain the highest level of ethics, integrity, and objectivity

Preferred Qualifications

Certified Public Accountant (CPA), Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) or equivalent certification

1-3 years of professional experience, preferably including internal audit or public accounting experience. Auditing work experience is preferred; however, business/operations experience may be deemed adequate.

Managerial courage to confront difficult issues with the appropriate response and to do so in a timely manner with any/all stakeholders

Comprehensive knowledge of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act provisions and methodologies for achieving compliance

Understanding of both current accounting (GAAP) and auditing (GAAS) principles

Strong interpersonal skills – ability to work closely with people at all levels of the organization

Proactive – demonstrated ability and desire to improve individual performance and advance the efficiency and effectiveness of the department

Ability to work in a highly complex environment under general direction as to assignment

Ability to solve conflict between differing priorities of various process stakeholders by offering pragmatic solutions to management

Ability to travel up to 30% to Cleveland-Cliffs locations as required

Data analytics and continuous auditing experience is preferred

ABOUT THINKING MACHINES

The mission of Thinking Machines is to build AI that extends human will and judgment. We are training frontier models with Inkling, developing Tinker to let people make models their own, and crafting interfaces that broaden human-AI communication. We believe the future worth building is human, and we're hiring people who want to build it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an infrastructure research engineer to design and build the core systems that enable scalable, efficient training of large models through reinforcement learning.

This role sits at the intersection of research and large-scale systems engineering: a builder who understands both the algorithms behind RL and the realities of distributed training and inference at scale. You’ll wear many hats, from optimizing rollout and reward pipelines to enhancing reliability, observability, and orchestration, collaborating closely with researchers and infra teams to make reinforcement learning stable, fast, and production-ready.

Note: This is an "evergreen role" that we keep open on an on-going basis to express interest. We receive many applications, and there may not always be an immediate role that aligns perfectly with your experience and skills. Still, we encourage you to apply. We continuously review applications and reach out to applicants as new opportunities open. You are welcome to reapply if you get more experience, but please avoid applying more than once every 6 months. You may also find that we put up postings for singular roles for separate, project or team specific needs. In those cases, you're welcome to apply directly in addition to an evergreen role.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design, build, and optimize the infrastructure that powers large-scale reinforcement learning and post-training workloads.

 - Improve the reliability and scalability of RL training pipeline, distributed RL workloads, and training throughput.

 - Develop shared monitoring and observability tools to ensure high uptime, debuggability, and reproducibility for RL systems.

 - Collaborate with researchers to translate algorithmic ideas into production-grade training pipelines.

 - Build evaluation and benchmarking infrastructure that measures model progress on helpfulness, safety, and factuality.

 - Publish and share learnings through internal documentation, open-source libraries, or technical reports that advance the field of scalable AI infrastructure.


SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum qualifications:

 - Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in computer science, electrical engineering, statistics, machine learning, physics, robotics, or similar.

 - Strong engineering skills, ability to contribute performant, maintainable code and debug in complex codebases

 - Understanding of deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, JAX) and their underlying system architectures.

 - Thrive in a highly collaborative environment involving many, different cross-functional partners and subject matter experts.

 - A bias for action with a mindset to take initiative to work across different stacks and different teams where you spot the opportunity to make sure something ships.

Preferred qualifications — we encourage you to apply if you meet some but not all of these:

 - Experience training or supporting large-scale language models with tens of billions of parameters or more.

 - Experience working with reinforcement learning workloads (e.g., PPO, DPO, RLHF, or reward modeling).

 - Background in high-performance or reliability engineering — distributed training frameworks and cluster orchestration (Kubernetes, Slurm).

 - Familiarity with monitoring and observability tools (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry).

 - Contributions to large-scale ML research or infrastructure, open-source frameworks, or internal performance optimization efforts.


LOGISTICS

 - Location: This role is based in San Francisco, California. 

 - Compensation: Depending on background, skills and experience, the expected annual salary range for this position is $425,000 - $475,000 USD.

 - Visa sponsorship: We sponsor visas. While we can't guarantee success for every candidate or role, if you're the right fit, we're committed to working through the visa process together.

 - Benefits: Thinking Machines offers generous health, dental, and vision benefits, unlimited PTO, paid parental leave, and relocation support as needed.
